general-information-environment-manageme.quote: **Evaluate** means judge the choices using evidence and reasons. Do not choose an option only because it sounds green or costs less.
general-information-environment-manageme.note: The rewrite now gives a local evidence-based method for comparing environmental alternatives.

general-information-environment-manageme.quote: People can affect ecosystems in several direct ways. Cutting or clearing habitat can remove food, shelter, or breeding places. Pollution can change water, soil, or air and make it harder for organisms to survive.
general-information-environment-manageme.note: The lesson now teaches causal human-impact mechanisms instead of only naming environmental programs.

general-information-environment-manageme.quote: Useful actions include protecting or restoring habitat, limiting harmful collection or trade, and reducing pollution or other pressures.
general-information-environment-manageme.note: The rewrite now supplies concrete species-conservation actions and ties action choice to the cause.

general-information-environment-manageme.quote: Good resource actions depend on the resource. They may include reducing waste, reusing materials, recycling, protecting source areas, restoring damaged places, or limiting harvest so a renewable resource has time to recover.
general-information-environment-manageme.note: The lesson now teaches several resource-conservation actions beyond waste sorting.

general-information-environment-manageme.quote: RA $9147$ also allows conservation breeding or propagation of threatened species. This work goes together with rehabilitation or protection of the habitat where the species may be released.
general-information-environment-manageme.note: RA $9147$ is now connected to a concrete threatened-species conservation action and habitat work.

general-information-environment-manageme.quote: A critical habitat is chosen using scientific data, including the presence of threatened species and pressures on their survival. Once designated, it must be protected from exploitation or destruction that can harm the threatened species that depend on it.
general-information-environment-manageme.note: The rewrite now explains the habitat-protection mechanism and why protection matters to threatened species.

general-information-environment-manageme.quote: NIPAS has protected-area categories such as strict nature reserve, natural park, natural monument, wildlife sanctuary, protected landscape or seascape, resource reserve, and natural biotic area. The category helps describe what kind of area is being protected.
general-information-environment-manageme.note: The rewrite now adds protected-area categories and later gives a worked local management action using zoning and restoration.

general-information-environment-manageme.quote: The action should match the cause of the problem.
general-information-environment-manageme.note: The lesson now teaches how to select a conservation action by matching it to the source of harm.

general-information-environment-manageme.quote: Taking wildlife or other resources too quickly can also cause harm. If a population or resource is removed faster than it can recover, less remains for the future.
general-information-environment-manageme.note: The rewrite now explains a cause-and-effect mechanism for human pressure on ecosystems and resources.

general-information-environment-manageme.quote: A **tradeoff** happens when one choice gives a benefit but also has a cost. A strong answer explains both sides and chooses the option that meets the goal with the least avoidable environmental harm.
general-information-environment-manageme.note: The lesson now explicitly teaches tradeoffs and an evidence-based rule for choosing among workable alternatives.
